name: Culli
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: ... mapas militares transcriben los nombres culle de lugar sin acento, excepto cuando la terminación es -gón. Ya que no sé dónde se sitúa el acento en cada caso particular, seguiré esta práctica. Dejo de lado los diacríticos empleados en la lista de Martínez Compañón porque su función es desconocida.
new_statements.translation: ... [the] military maps transcribe the Culle place names without an accent mark, except when the ending is -gón. Since I do not know where the accent falls in each particular case, I shall follow this practice. I leave aside the diacritics used in Martínez Compañón's list because their function is unknown.

new_statements.locator: p. 100 (orthographic conventions for citing Culle toponyms and the Martínez Compañón list)

new_statements.rule_in_words: No stress rule is recoverable: the principal modern analyst of Culli states that the position of the accent in Culle forms is unknown to him and that the diacritics (grave accents etc.) in the 18th-century Martínez Compañón word list, the only source that marks anything, are of unknown function. The one orthographic regularity (Spanish acute on toponyms in -gón, e.g. Chusgón) is a map-spelling convention for hispanicised place names, not a claim about Culli word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Toponyms ending in -gón are written with a (final) accent on Peruvian military maps; Adelaar adopts this spelling without endorsing it as Culli stress. Later work (Adelaar & Muysken 2004: 402 as cited by Andrade 2016; Urban 2025: 586) reads the grave-accented final <-ù> of the verbs in Martínez Compañón's list as an infinitive marker /u/~/w/, not as a stress mark; Urban 2019: 79, 104 fn.103 likewise finds the plan's diacritics unexplained and the grave-as-stress reading doubtful.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns citation of toponyms and word-list items of an extinct language known from c. 60 lexical items; no phrase- vs word-level distinction is possible. Passage reconstructed from overlapping Google Books snippets (snippet view volume), not from a full page image.
new_statements.identity_note: Culli = Culle/Kulyi/Ilinga (Glottolog cull1235, no ISO). All sources treat the Huamachuco material (Martínez Compañón, 1780s) and the Pallasca material (Gonzales 1915 via Rivet 1949) as one language; no dialect differentiation is possible. The quoted statement is about the language as a whole (toponyms + word list), not a particular variety.

sources.note: p.100: military maps write Culle place names without accent marks except for the ending -gón; 'Ya que no sé dónde se sitúa el acento en cada caso particular, seguiré esta práctica'; the diacritics in Martínez Compañón's Culle list are set aside 'porque su función es desconocida'. I.e. the leading authority states that accent placement is unknown/unrecoverable.

sources.note: p.79: the diacritics in Martínez Compañón's 'plan' are unexplained ('their significance is unclear'), incl. a star-like diacritic found only in the Culli and Mochica lists; p.104 fn.103: reading the grave accent (as in Sechura <tutù>, <chùpchùp>) as a primary-stress mark is doubtful.
